outcomes.title: Strong Prosecutable Case
outcomes.description: The investigation identifies the responsible person, establishes the core homicide elements through multiple independent routes, preserves strong corroborating evidence, and avoids material procedural damage.

outcomes.title: Insufficient Evidence
outcomes.description: The submitted theory may be plausible, but the investigation does not establish enough of the required offense elements or admissible corroboration to support prosecution.

outcomes.title: Correct Theory, Damaged Case
outcomes.description: The investigation identifies substantial evidence pointing toward the responsible person, but material procedural mistakes weaken or suppress important evidence.

outcomes.title: Wrong Primary Suspect
outcomes.description: The submitted case identifies a person who is not canonically responsible for the homicide.

outcomes.title: Incomplete Responsibility Theory
outcomes.description: The submitted theory fails to identify all materially responsible participants in a case where multiple participants exist.

outcomes.title: Prosecutor Declines Charges
outcomes.description: The investigation contains meaningful suspicion but not enough legally usable evidence to justify filing the primary homicide charge.

outcomes.title: Reduced Charging Decision
outcomes.description: The evidence supports criminal responsibility but leaves material weaknesses in proof, admissibility, or offense-element support. The prosecutor elects a reduced charging posture.

outcomes.title: Acquittal
outcomes.description: The investigation reaches prosecution, but evidentiary weakness, suppression, or insufficient corroboration prevents proof beyond a reasonable doubt.

outcomes.title: Conviction
outcomes.description: The investigation produces a legally sound and sufficiently corroborated prosecution resulting in conviction.

outcomes.title: Case Remains Unsolved
outcomes.description: The player submits without establishing a sufficiently supported and prosecutable theory.
